question:
A 21-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician for evaluation of malaise, joint pains, and rash. She has developed joint pain in her hands over the last month, and has noted a rash over her face that gets worse with sun exposure. She is taking no medication at the present time. On further physical examination, an erythematous rash with a small amount of underlying edema is seen on her face. Her complete blood count is remarkable due to a lymphocytopenia. What are other disorders known to cause lymphocytopenia?
I 22q.11.2 deletion syndrome
II Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) defect
III Diphyllobothrium latum infection
IV Whole body radiation
V Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lymphocytopenia" -> "associated with immunodeficiency disorders" -> "22q.11.2 deletion syndrome known to cause immunodeficiency" -> "Bruton tyrosine kinase defect causes X-linked agammaglobulinemia" -> "Diphyllobothrium latum infection typically causes eosinophilia" -> "Whole body radiation leads to lymphocyte depletion" -> "Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome primarily affects platelet function" -> "I, II, IV are relevant" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Lymphocytopenia" -> "can result from genetic disorders" -> "22q.11.2 deletion syndrome linked to T-cell deficiency" -> "Bruton tyrosine kinase defect leads to B-cell deficiency" -> "Diphyllobothrium latum infection does not typically cause lymphocytopenia" -> "Whole body radiation causes lymphocyte loss" -> "Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome does not cause lymphocytopenia" -> "I, II, IV are relevant" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Lymphocytopenia" -> "can be caused by infections" -> "Diphyllobothrium latum infection is not associated with lymphocytopenia" -> "can be caused by radiation exposure" -> "Whole body radiation leads to lymphocyte depletion" -> "22q.11.2 deletion syndrome and BTK defect are known causes" -> "Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome is unrelated" -> "I, II, IV are relevant" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Lymphocytopenia" -> "can be due to various causes" -> "22q.11.2 deletion syndrome causes immunodeficiency" -> "Bruton tyrosine kinase defect leads to B-cell deficiency" -> "Diphyllobothrium latum infection typically causes eosinophilia" -> "Whole body radiation results in lymphocyte loss" -> "Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome affects platelets, not lymphocytes" -> "I, II, IV are relevant" -> 75%
analysis: Lymphocytopenia can be caused by a variety of conditions. In this case, we need to evaluate each option: I (22q.11.2 deletion syndrome) is known to cause immunodeficiency and can lead to lymphocytopenia. II (Bruton tyrosine kinase defect) is associated with X-linked agammaglobulinemia, which also results in lymphocytopenia due to impaired B-cell development. III (Diphyllobothrium latum infection) typically causes macrocytic anemia and is not directly associated with lymphocytopenia. IV (Whole body radiation) can lead to lymphocytopenia due to damage to the bone marrow and lymphoid tissues. V (Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome) is a bleeding disorder related to platelet function and does not typically cause lymphocytopenia. Therefore, the correct answer includes I, II, and IV, which are known to cause lymphocytopenia. The best-supported option is opd (I, II, IV, V) as it includes all relevant conditions except for the unrelated Glanzmann-Riniker syndrome.
